article.story: OXFORD, Miss. -- — Jada Richard scored 15 of her career-high 22 points in the second half, and she also had five rebounds and six assists as No. 19 Mississippi beat Alabama A&M 66-47 on Sunday. Talaysia Cooper added 15 points for Ole Miss (5-1). Cooper was 4 of 11 from 3-point range and Richard added three makes, while the rest of their teammates combined to go 0 for 6. Janessa Kelley led Alabama A&M (2-5) with 12 points on four 3-pointers. The teams got off to a slow start in the first quarter, combining for 11 turnovers and both shooting under 30% from the field. It was more of the same in the second quarter, with Ole Miss leading 26-21 at the break despite shooting 32% including 2 of 12 from distance. The Rebels had 11 turnovers in the first half and Alabama A&M 12. Richard made two 3-pointers during a 9-0 run that ended with Ole Miss in front 57-41 midway through the fourth. The Rebels stayed ahead by double figures the rest of the way. The game featured 39 turnovers and both teams shot under 55% from the free-throw line, with Ole Miss going 13 of 24 and Alabama A&M 4 of 9.
